Rashi on Yevamot 36a:10:1.hebrew: ולטעמיך - אי טעמא דלא תחלוץ משום ספק מעוברת צרתה בשעת חליצה היא, תחלוץ לאחר ט' — דהשתא ודאי לאו מעוברת היא — ותנשא; ומ"ט קתני "עד שתדע", ואפי' לסוף כמה שנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:10:1.english: And according to your reasoning - If the reason that she may not perform ḥalitza is because her co-wife is possibly pregnant at the time of ḥalitza, let her perform ḥalitza after nine [months] — for now she is certainly not pregnant — and marry; and what is the reason [the mishna] teaches "until she knows," even at the end of several years?

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:11:1.hebrew: אלא בר מינה דההיא - כלומר, מההיא לא תידוק סייעתא לר"ל, דהא דקתני לא תחלוץ בתוך ט' ותנשא לאחר ט', התם טעמא לאו משום ספק יבמה לשוק הוא, אלא כדאביי בר אבין כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:11:1.english: Rather, [leave] that [mishna] out of it - That is to say, do not infer support for Reish Lakish from that [mishna], for [regarding] that which it teaches, "she may not perform ḥalitza within nine [months] and [then] marry after nine [months]" — there, the reason is not because of [a concern of] a possible yevama [marrying] into the general public; rather, [it is] as Abaye bar Avin etc. [stated].

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:11:2.english: Perhaps there will be an offspring - [of] her rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:11:3.hebrew: בן קיימא - ונמצא חליצתה שלא לצורך, וכשרה לכהונה. ומי שראה בחליצה מחזיקה כפסולה לכהונה, ואתה צריך להכריז, "דעו שזו לא פסלתה חליצתה":
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:11:3.english: Viable - And [thus] her chalitzah turns out to be unnecessary, and she is fit for the priesthood. Yet whoever witnessed the chalitzah presumes her to be disqualified from the priesthood, and you must announce, "Know that her chalitzah did not disqualify this woman."

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:13:1.hebrew: [א"ל] אביי מידי לא תחלוץ ולא תתייבם קתני - דתידוק מינה סייעתא לר"ל:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:13:1.english: Abaye said to him: Does [the Mishnah] teach, "She may neither perform chalitzah nor enter into levirate marriage"? - That you should infer from it a support for Reish Lakish.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:13:2.hebrew: לא תנשא קתני - דלא תנשא לשוק בלא חליצה, לסמוך ולומר "צרתי ילדה לבעלי", אע"פ שרוב נשים יולדות. אבל אי חלצה אפי' בתוך ט', ה"נ דמשתריא לאחר ט', דביאת מעוברת וחליצתה שמה ביאה וחליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:13:2.english: It teaches, "She may not be married" - That she may not marry [an outsider] without ḥalitza, relying [on the assumption] and saying, "My co-wife has borne a child to my husband," even though most women give birth. However, if she performed ḥalitza even within nine [months], so too she is permitted [to marry] after nine [months], for the intercourse of a pregnant woman and her ḥalitza are considered [valid] intercourse and ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:15:1.hebrew: על פיו - אחרי דברי פיו, ולא בסתם ירושה בשתיקה:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:15:1.english: By his mouth - Following the words of his mouth, and not through ordinary inheritance in silence.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:15:2.hebrew: ריבה לאחד ומיעט לאחד או שהשוה לו את הבכור דבריו קיימים - דלכולן נתן בחייו, ואין כאן ירושה ליטול בכורה, ולא הפשוטים ליטול בשוה, אלא מה שריבה ריבה, ומה שמיעט מיעט:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:15:2.english: [If] he increased [the share] for one and decreased [it] for one, or made the firstborn equal to him, his words stand - For he gave [his property] to all of them during his lifetime, and there is no inheritance here [for the firstborn] to take a firstborn's [double] portion, nor [for] the ordinary [sons] to take equally; rather, what he increased, he increased, and what he decreased, he decreased.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:16:1.english: And if he said [it] as an inheritance - [Meaning, he said:] "So-and-so shall inherit such-and-such a field, and so-and-so [shall inherit] such-and-such a field."

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:16:2.hebrew: לא אמר כלום - שהתנה על מה שכתוב בתורה ותנאו בטל, הואיל ולא חילק לפשוטים בשוה ולבכור פי שנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:16:2.english: He said nothing - For he stipulated contrary to what is written in the Torah, and his stipulation is void, since he did not divide [the estate] equally among the ordinary [sons] and [give] a double portion to the firstborn.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:16:3.english: At the beginning - "Let such-and-such a field be given to so-and-so, and he shall inherit it."

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:16:4.english: In the middle - "[Let him] inherit it, and let it be given to him, and [let him] inherit it."

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:16:5.english: At the end - [He wrote:] "Let him inherit it, and let it be given to him."

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:1:1.english: That anyone who is eligible for levirate marriage, etc. - For her intercourse exempts her.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:1:2.english: Is eligible for ḥalitza - As it is written (Deuteronomy 25:7): "If the man does not wish to take his brother's wife, then she shall remove [his shoe]," etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:2:1.hebrew: שמא יהא הולד של קיימא וביאת מעוברת - בולד של קיימא, לדברי הכל לא שמה ביאה, דטעמא דרבי יוחנן משום שמא יבא אליהו ויאמר נפל הואי, והכא ליכא למימר הכי. והולד אין פוטר עד שיצא לאויר העולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:2:1.english: Lest the child be viable, and intercourse with a pregnant woman - [In the case of] a viable child, according to everyone it is not considered [valid] intercourse, for Rabbi Yochanan's reason is lest Elijah come and say it was a miscarriage, and here it is not possible to say so. And the child does not exempt [her] until it emerges into the air of the world.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:4:1.hebrew: הא לא יהא ולד של קיימא - דלמפרע בת יבום היא, הוה מיפטרא צרתה, ואין צריך לחזור ולבעול לאחר שהפילה:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:4:1.english: [If] the offspring will not be viable - [since] retroactively she is subject to levirate marriage, her rival wife would be released, and he does not need to have intercourse [with her] again after she miscarried.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:5:1.hebrew: אמר לך ר"ל הכי קתני - כלומר, לא קתני "שמא יהא", אלא "שמא לא יהא". והאי דקתני סיפא "ולד אינו פוטר כו'", דמשמע דבשל קיימא מיירי, הכי קאמר: וא"ת, הלך אחר רוב נשים, ורוב נשים ולד מעליא ילדן, ונהי דביאתה לא פטרה, מיהו פטורה משום הולד — הולד אין פוטר עד שיצא לאויר העולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:5:1.english: Reish Lakish [could have] said to you: This is what [the baraita] teaches - That is to say, it does not teach "lest [the offspring] be [viable]," rather "lest [the offspring] not be [viable]." And that which the latter clause [of the baraita] teaches, "the offspring does not exempt, etc.," which implies that it is dealing with a viable [offspring], this is what it means: And if you say, follow the majority of women, and the majority of women give birth to a healthy offspring, and granted that her intercourse does not exempt [her], nevertheless she is exempt on account of the offspring — [the baraita teaches that] the offspring does not exempt until it emerges into the air of the world.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:7:1.english: Whose husband went - And he has no children.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:7:2.hebrew: לא תנשא - קס"ד אפילו ע"י חליצה קאמר, דלא תנשא לשוק לעולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:7:2.english: She may not marry - It was initially assumed [that the Mishnah] means even through ḥalitzah, that she may never marry an outsider.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:7:3.hebrew: היא צרתה - אותה צרתה שהלכה עמו. אבל אי שמעה עליה שאינה מעוברת, תתייבם, ולא חיישינן שמא נשא בעלה אחרת במדינת הים. ולהכי תנן היא צרתה, והכי מפרש בפ' האשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:7:3.english: She, her rival wife - [That is,] that rival wife of hers who went with him. However, if she heard about her that she is not pregnant, she may enter into levirate marriage, and we do not suspect that perhaps her husband married another [woman] overseas. And for this reason [the Mishnah] taught "she, her rival wife," and so it is explained in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:1.english: Rather, she may not perform chalitzah - and marry an outsider.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:2.hebrew: אמאי - אי חליצת מעוברת שמה חליצה, תחלוץ ממה נפשך, דבין צרתה מעוברת ובין אינה מעוברת, הרי חליצה פוטרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:2.english: Why - If the ḥalitza of a pregnant woman is considered [valid] ḥalitza, let her perform ḥalitza either way, for whether her rival wife is pregnant or is not pregnant, ḥalitza releases her.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:3.hebrew: בשלמא תחלוץ בתוך ג' ותנשא בתוך ג' - שמת:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:3.english: Granted, she may perform chalitzah within three [months] and marry within three [months] - [after he] died.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:4.hebrew: לא - אפשר דהיינו ספק דבן ט' לראשון או בן ז' לאחרון, דאפילו נשאת ב' ימים בתוך ג' חדשים וילדה בסוף ט' לבעל הראשון, אכתי איכא למימר שמא בן ז' לאחרון הוא, ואע"פ שאין אלא ו' חדשים וב' ימים, דקי"ל (ר"ה דף יא.): יולדת לז' — יולדת למקוטעין. ואע"ג דהיא לאו ודאי מעוברת — דהא מדקתני "שמא מעוברת צרתה", מכלל דאחר זמן מרובה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים קמיירי — לא פלוג רבנן בנשים, אלא כולן צריכות להמתין:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:4.english: No - It is possible that this is the uncertainty of [whether the child is] a nine-month [child] of the first [husband] or a seven-month [child] of the latter [husband]. For even if she married two days within [the] three months [waiting period] and gave birth at the end of nine [months] from the first husband, there is still room to say perhaps it is a seven-month [child] of the latter [husband], even though there are only six months and two days [since the second marriage], for we hold (Rosh Hashanah 11a) [that] a woman who gives birth at seven [months] can give birth in incomplete [months]. And even though she is not definitely pregnant — for since it teaches "perhaps her rival wife is pregnant," it follows by implication that it is speaking of after a long time when her husband had gone overseas — the Sages did not differentiate among women; rather, all of them must wait.

Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:5.hebrew: אלא תחלוץ בתוך ג' ותנשא לאחר כו' - וקשה לי: היכי מצי לאותובי הכי? נהי נמי דחליצת מעוברת שמה חליצה, הני מילי בנפל, אבל הכא הא איכא למיחש שמא צרתה מעוברת בולד בן קיימא, ואין ביאה וחליצה פוטרת בה לדברי הכל אלא ולד, והולד אין פוטר עד שיצא לאויר העולם. ונראה בעיני דה"ג: בשלמא תחלוץ בתוך ט' ותנשא בתוך ט' — לא, דהיינו ספק, שמא יהא ולד צרתה בן קיימא, ואין ביאה וחליצה פוטרת אלא ולד, והולד אין פוטר עד שיצא לאויר העולם, ול"ג אי בן ט' לראשון, ופירושו היה בספרים משובשים. אלא תחלוץ בתוך ט' ותנשא לאחר ט' — ממה נפשך: אי מיעברא צרתה והפילה, או לאו מעוברת הואי, הרי חלצה זו; ואי ולד של קיימא הוה, הרי יצא לאויר העולם! אלא לאו משום שמא מעוברת צרתה היתה בשעת חליצה ואין הולד של קיימא, וההיא חליצה לא פטרה, כר"ל — הואיל ואחת מהן מעוברת, לא שייכא חליצה ההיא שעתא, דאמרינן: עיין עליו:
Rashi on Yevamot 36a:8:5.english: Rather, let her perform ḥalitza within three [months] and marry after [three months], etc. - And it is difficult for me: how can [the Gemara] raise an objection like this? Even though the ḥalitza of a pregnant woman is considered a valid ḥalitza, that applies only in [the case of] a non-viable fetus; but here, surely there is reason to be concerned lest her rival wife is pregnant with a viable child, and neither levirate marriage nor ḥalitza exempts her according to all opinions — only a child [exempts her], and a child does not exempt [her] until it emerges into the air of the world! And it appears to me that this is how we read [the Gemara]: "Granted, let her perform ḥalitza within nine [months] and marry within nine [months] — no, for this is [a case of] uncertainty, lest her rival wife's child be viable, and neither levirate marriage nor ḥalitza exempts [her], only a child, and the child does not exempt [her] until it emerges into the air of the world" — and we do not read: "whether [it is] a nine-[month child] of the first [husband]," and its explanation was in corrupt texts — "Rather, let her perform ḥalitza within nine [months] and marry after nine [months]!" Either way [she should be permitted to marry]: if her rival wife was pregnant and miscarried, or if she was not pregnant, behold, this [woman] has performed ḥalitza; and if it was a viable child, behold, it has [already] emerged into the air of the world! Rather, is it not because [we are concerned] lest her rival wife was pregnant at the time of the ḥalitza and the child is not viable, and that ḥalitza does not exempt [her], in accordance with Reish Lakish — [that] since one of them is pregnant, ḥalitza does not apply at that time, as we say: "Examine it carefully!"

Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:11:1.hebrew: ונמצא אתה מצריכה כרוז לכהונה - ודוקא בשאר נשים דלאו גרושות איירי, וכן מוקי לה בהדיא בפרק בתרא (לקמן יבמות קיט: ושם). והא דפריך לקמן (יבמות דף מא:) גבי "והיבמה לא תחלוץ עד שיהא לה ג' חדשים" ומפרש בגמרא מעיקרא טעמא "שמא יהא ולד של קיימא ונמצא מצריכה כרוז לכהונה" — תינח אלמנה, גרושה מאי איכא למימר? אר"י: משום דהתם בא להשמיענו דין כל הנשים שנופלות לייבום, ואם היה דין אחר לגרושה ה"ל לפרושי; אבל הכא, דאיירי אם אירע בו מעשה באשה שהלך בעלה וצרתה למדינת הים, איירי שפיר דוקא בשאר נשים דלאו גרושות. ועדיפא מינה בפרק בתרא, דמוקי ההיא ד"האשה שלום" דוקא בגרושה, דפריך מינה אההיא דמייתי הכא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:11:1.english: "And it would emerge that you will require a public announcement for her to [marry into] the priesthood" - This refers specifically to other women who are not divorcees, and indeed [the Gemara] establishes it explicitly so in the last chapter (below, Yevamot 119b and there). And as for that which [the Gemara] asks below (Yevamot 41b) regarding [the Mishnah]: "A yevamah may not perform ḥalitza until she has [waited] three months," where the Gemara initially explains the reason [as being] "perhaps the offspring will be viable, and it would emerge that you require a public announcement for her [to marry] into the priesthood" — [asking:] "That is well for a widow; what is there to say for a divorcee?" — Ri said: Because there [the Mishnah] comes to teach us the law of all women who fall [before a brother-in-law] for levirate marriage, and if there were a different law for a divorcee, it should have specified [it]; whereas here, where it is speaking of a case where an incident occurred involving a woman whose husband and co-wife went overseas, it properly speaks specifically of other women who are not divorcees. And even stronger than this is [the case] in the last chapter, where [the Gemara] establishes that [Mishnah] of "HaIsha Shalom" specifically regarding a divorcee, from which it raises an objection against that [statement] which it cites here.

Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:15:1.hebrew: הלכתא כר"ל בהני תלת - הא דפליגי בפרק ב' דחולין (דף כט: ושם) גבי "ישנה לשחיטה מתחלה ועד סוף", לא חשיב הכא אע"ג דסבירא ליה כוותיה בפ' ב' דזבחים (דף ל. ושם) — היינו משום דר"ל משמיה דלוי סבא אמרה. ותימה דלא חשיב הא דפ"ק דמסכת ע"ז (דף ו: ושם) דתניא כותיה דר"ל, דנשא ונתן מותר, כיון דחשיב הכא מידי דתניא כוותיה. ואור"י דמ"מ התם הלכתא כר' יוחנן, דהתם גבי הא דתנן: "וחכ"א לפניהם אסור, לאחריהם מותר", פריך: "חכמים היינו ת"ק", ומשני: "נשא ונתן איכא בינייהו". ובפרק קמא דסנהדרין (דף טו: ושם) גבי זאב וארי, דתניא כוותיה דר"ל — התם פליגי אליבא דר"א, ולא סבירא להו כוותיה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:15:1.english: "The halakha is in accordance with Reish Lakish in these three" - That [dispute] in which they disagree in the second chapter of Chullin (29b and there) regarding [the principle that] "the process of slaughter extends from the beginning to the end" is not counted here—even though [Rava] holds in accordance with him in the second chapter of Zevachim (30a and there)—because Reish Lakish stated it in the name of Levi Sava. And it is astonishing that he does not count that [dispute] of the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (6b and there), where a baraita is taught in accordance with Reish Lakish that [if] one transacted, it is permitted—since here he counts something where a baraita is taught in accordance with him! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that nevertheless, there the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan; for there, regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah: "And the Sages say: Before their [festivals] it is forbidden; after them it is permitted," [the Gemara] asks: "The Sages" is identical to the first tanna! And it answers: "[The case where] he transacted is [the difference] between them." And [as for the dispute] in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (15b and there) regarding a wolf and a lion, where a baraita is taught in accordance with Reish Lakish—there they disagree according to Rabbi Eliezer, and they themselves do not hold in accordance with him.

Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:16:1.hebrew: משום ירושה לא אמר כלום - טעמא מפרש התם במתניתין: לפי שהתנה על מה שכתוב בתורה. ורבי יוחנן בן ברוקא פליג בפרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב קל.), ואמר דאם אמר על מי שראוי ליורשו — דבריו קיימים. וטעמא מפרש התם, משום דכתיב "והיה ביום הנחילו את בניו" — התורה נתנה רשות לאב להנחיל לכל מי שירצה. והא דכתיב "לא יוכל לבכר" — היינו דוקא חלק בכורה, אבל חלק פשיטות יכול. ורבנן "ביום הנחילו את בניו" מוקמי לדרשא אחריתי, ו"לא יוכל לבכר" איצטריך משום דהורע כחו שאין נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק, וס"ד דהורע כחו נמי בהא; א"נ איצטריך דס"ד כיון דשנואה, שנואה בנישואיה, דיכול לבכר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:16:1.english: As an inheritance, he has said nothing - The reason is explained there in the Mishnah: because he stipulated contrary to what is written in the Torah. And Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka disagrees in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Noḥalin (Bava Batra 130a), and says that if he said [this] regarding one who is fit to inherit him, his words stand. And the reason is explained there: because it is written, "And it shall be on the day he bequeaths to his sons" [Deuteronomy 21:16] — the Torah gave permission to a father to bequeath to whomever he wishes. And that which is written, "he may not treat as firstborn" — that refers specifically to the firstborn's portion, whereas [regarding] an ordinary portion he is able [to do so]. And the Rabbis establish "on the day he bequeaths to his sons" for a different exposition, and "he may not treat as firstborn" is needed because [the firstborn's] power is diminished in that he does not take [a double portion] in prospective [assets] as in already-possessed [assets], and you might have thought that his power is diminished in this [case] as well; alternatively, it is needed because you might have thought that since [she is] "hated" — [meaning] hated in her marriage — he is able to treat [the other son] as firstborn:

Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:8:1.hebrew: בשלמא בתוך ג' חדשים כו' - אין גירסא זו נכונה כדפירש בקונטרס. ועוד, דאי אפשר כלל לדקדק מדאינה חולצת תוך ג' לינשא אחר ג' דחליצת מעוברת לא שמה חליצה, דהא ודאי תוך ג' מודה ר' יוחנן דאין חולצת, כדתנן: "היבמה לא תחלוץ עד שיהיו לה ג' חדשים". וטעמא משום דאינה עולה לייבום, דאפי' יבא אליהו ויאמר דלא מיעברא לאו בת ייבום היא, ולכך אינה עולה לחליצה. אבל בתוך ט' בת ייבום היא אם יבא אליהו ויאמר דלא מיעברא או אפילו הפילה, לכך דייק שפיר. אלא ה"ג: "תחלוץ בתוך ט' ותנשא לאחר ט'":
Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:8:1.english: Granted, within three months, etc. - This textual reading is not correct, as Rashi explained. Furthermore, it is completely impossible to infer from [the fact] that she does not perform chalitzah within three [months] [in order] to marry after three [months] that the chalitzah of a pregnant woman is not considered chalitzah — for certainly within three [months] Rabbi Yochanan agrees that she does not perform chalitzah, as we learned in the Mishnah: "The yevamah may not perform chalitzah until she has [waited] three months." And the reason is because she is not eligible for yibbum, for even if Elijah were to come and say that she is not pregnant, she is not fit for yibbum, and therefore she is not eligible for chalitzah. However, within nine [months] she is fit for yibbum if Elijah were to come and say that she is not pregnant, or even if she miscarried; therefore [the Gemara] infers well. Rather, this is how we read [the text]: "She should perform chalitzah within nine [months] and marry after nine [months]."

Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:8:2.hebrew: ותנשא לאחר ט' - תימה, דלא מסיק אדעתיה האי "ולטעמיך" דפריך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 36a:8:2.english: And marry after nine [months] - It is astonishing that [Rabbi Elazar] did not think of this [objection of] "and according to your reasoning" that [the Gemara] asks.
